output.brief: The complaints are very likely caused by water-contaminated brake fluid put in at Northfield Motor Services while Eastgate's own brake bay was closed. 11 of the 13 vans Northfield serviced produced all 27 complaints, and the two that got fluid from a fresh drum had none. The Northfield stock drum had been open since March and its cap went missing. Two returned vans tested at 149–152°C boiling point, against 255°C for sealed stock. Calder Road and in-house vans ran the same Upper Wend routes for similar numbers of days and had no complaints. The same drivers also had no reports in other vans. So driver technique, the Tessaro pads and easier reporting don't explain it. The hills are where the weak fluid shows up, not the cause. Do not discipline the drivers. They reported a real hazard, and the garage's 25 Sep warning went unanswered. This week: take the remaining Northfield-serviced vans off the road, test the fluid and renew it from sealed stock, then return them to service. Also look at the fluid Calder Road used. Reverting pad supplier for squeal is not justified yet. I'm fairly confident, though I haven't seen the fluid tests on the other vans.
